subject: Re: Next steps for deployment mode and migration plan - Nova Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novahealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop, logan_wright
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps  deployment mode & migration plan (post-call recap)

Thanks again for taking the call today, Samir  great to meet you and hear more about Nova Health's roadmap for embedding LLM capabilities into your clinician workflows. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from call:
- Current state: experimenting with a mix of OpenAI-hosted APIs and an internal GPU cluster for privacy-sensitive workloads.
- Key constraints: PHI/data residency, predictable latency for real-time suggestions, and cost predictability at scale.
- Primary goal: pilot a production inference path for triage & summarization that meets compliance and latency SLOs.

Deployment options we discussed (high-level):
1) Hosted API (Redwood-hosted): fastest to ship, simplest integration. Good for non-PHI or aggregated data.
2) Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools (SLA-backed) in our cloud region with customer isolation. Best fit if you want production latency and cost predictability without on-prem ops.
3) Private VPC / on-prem: customer-managed network and optional on-prem package for strict compliance/regulatory needs (can integrate with KMS/HSM).

Migration considerations raised today:
- Migration from OpenAI/API-first approach: model mapping, prompt parity, and inference latency differences.
- Migration from legacy GPU cluster (self-hosted): model conversion, quantization compatibility, and moving KV cache/prefix state for warm-up.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- Technical deep-dive with Logan (SE) to scope migration steps (recommend 60–90 min). Options: Wed 5/12 or Thu 5/13.
- Procurement: start SOW template + estimate for 3-month pilot (Lauren to lead).
- Deliverables from Redwood: deployment options doc (attached), proposed pilot scope, and a mutual action plan link below.

Attachments: redwood-deployment-options.pdf (summary), Mutual Action Plan (Drive link)

Would you confirm which date works for the technical deep-dive and if we should include your infra/SEC contacts on the call?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@novahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Cc: lauren_bishop
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Technical deep-dive  migration notes and checklist

Hi Samir  quick note ahead of the technical call. Based on the attached infra diagram, here's a practical checklist and what we'll cover on the deep-dive: 

Migration paths we typically use:
- From external APIs (OpenAI):
  - Validate prompt parity and sampling/temperature behavior with model variants.
  - Test response latency differences and set batching/timeout configs.
  - Map rate limits and design fallbacks for throttling.
- From self-hosted/legacy GPU clusters:
  - Confirm model weights and format (PyTorch vs TorchScript) and apply quantization profiles if needed.
  - KV cache & prefix state: plan for pre-warming frequently used prefixes to avoid cold-start latency.
  - Data egress/security: define ingress/outbound rules and KMS integration for any keys.

What I need from Nova Health prior to the call:
- Example prompts and expected response sizes (tokens).
- A short sample of latencies from your current cluster/OpenAI calls.
- Any compliance checklist items (e.g., SOC2 sections, retention windows) we should pre-validate.

On the call we'll walk through a concrete migration runbook: staging -> pilot -> production, rollback criteria, and performance targets.

Available windows: Tue 5/18 10:00–12:00 or Thu 5/20 14:00–16:00 PT. Which would work?

Cheers,
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.ai
